mcat_description.short: Portable Toilets are prefabricated, self-contained sanitation cabin units made from FRP, HDPE, MS, or PVC, sold per piece for temporary or semi-permanent deployment at construction sites, events, highways, and public spaces.
mcat_description.long: Portable Toilets in the Indian B2B market are factory-built cabin units constructed from Fibre Reinforced Plastic (FRP), High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE), Mild Steel (MS), or PVC panels, available in Indian squat-pan and Western commode styles, with optional bio-digester, septic tank, or chemical waste management systems. Units range from single-seater economical cabins to multi-compartment labour toilet blocks, mobile toilet vans, and executive restroom units, with built-in overhead water tanks, ventilation, electrical fittings, and anti-skid flooring as standard or optional features. Key demand drivers include compliance with the Building and Other Construction Workers (BOCW) Act mandating on-site sanitation, Swachh Bharat Mission government procurement, and large-scale infrastructure and event projects requiring rapid, relocatable sanitation deployment. Buyers include construction contractors, event management companies, municipal corporations, highway authorities, and labour camp operators who procure in single units or bulk lots.

market_context: The Indian portable toilet market is dominated by FRP (Fibre Reinforced Plastic) cabin-style units, with HDPE, MS, and PVC as secondary materials; FRP is preferred for its corrosion resistance, light weight, and weather durability in Indian outdoor conditions. Two primary style variants exist across all material types: Indian squat-pan (more common in labour/construction segment) and Western commode (preferred for events and executive use). Bio-digester portable toilets — which use microbial cultures to treat waste without requiring sewage connection or frequent manual emptying — are a significant and growing sub-segment driven by Swachh Bharat Mission government procurement and BOCW Act compliance mandates for construction sites. Key manufacturing hubs are Pune (Maharashtra), Ahmedabad (Gujarat), Thane/Mumbai, and Hyderabad, with pan-India supply. Buyers typically procure in bulk (10–100+ units) for construction projects or government tenders, and single units for events or small sites. The BOCW (Building and Other Construction Workers) Act legally mandates on-site sanitation facilities, making construction contractors a captive buyer segment. Sintex is a recognised trade name in this category; most supply is from unbranded regional FRP fabricators. Units are sold both outright (purchase) and on rental/AMC basis for event and municipal use.
